name: instant-worker — customer backup FAILED (credential/auth) [SLA breach]
description:
Page when a per-tenant (customer) backup run fails with reason='auth' — i.e. pg_dump was rejected by the customer's Postgres (password authentication failed / role missing / permission denied). This means the stored connection_url credential has drifted from the live DB role; it will NOT self-heal and every scheduled backup for that resource keeps failing, so the paid-tier durability/SLA promise is broken for any data written since the last good backup.

Why this alert exists: the pre-existing backup alerts MISS a clean failure — backup-stale-36h.json only fires after 36h of no success (far too slow for an SLA breach), and backup-requested-no-followup.json only fires on STUCK rows (a prompt failure emits backup.failed so it counts as 'followed up'). A failed backup previously paged no one promptly. (Source: worker markFailed slog line jobs.customer_backup_runner.failed with structured field reason; metric instant_customer_backup_failed_total{reason="auth"}.)

When this fires:
  1. Identify the resource: NR Logs `service='worker' message LIKE '%customer_backup_runner.failed%' reason='auth'` — the line carries backup_id + internal_detail (the raw pg_dump stderr, with the role name).
  2. Confirm drift: decrypt resources.connection_url for that resource and test a real login against the customer Postgres. If the role rejects it, the stored credential is stale.
  3. Re-sync the credential (re-provision the role password or update the stored connection_url) — do NOT auto-rotate blindly (it can break the customer's live app).
  4. Re-run the backup once fixed: it will pick up on the next scheduled tick or via a manual enqueue.
  See infra/BACKUP-RESTORE-RUNBOOK.md. The customer-facing message is sanitized (no host/role leak); full detail is in the worker log only.

nrql.query: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE service = 'worker' AND message LIKE '%customer_backup_runner.failed%' AND reason = 'auth'
